description: The bound on hung punctuation. A line ending in a full stop or a closing quote sets that mark outside the paragraph box rather than wrapping it, which is what every Chinese typesetter does and what the line breaker already did: a hung unit is exempt from the width check that decides where a line ends. The exemption had no ceiling, so a run of hung units -- a full stop and the closing quote after it are two, and both are in the hung set -- accumulated one em each past the box edge, and a page that draws a column rule a few points beyond the box had text struck through by it. hang_max_em is that ceiling. It is the furthest past the box's right edge a hung unit may be set, counted from the edge to the unit's own right side, so a run of them is bounded by where the last one ends rather than by how many there are. It is written in ems of the paragraph's dominant font size rather than in points, so the same declaration bounds a caption and a pull quote alike. Where the ceiling is exceeded the line does not simply wrap the offending mark: wrapping it alone would open the next line with punctuation, which is the violation the hung set exists to prevent. Instead the trailing run of hung units is pulled back on to the next line together with the one unit before it, so the new line opens with the character that mark belongs to. The retreat is bounded by construction -- it is never longer than the hung run plus one -- and it is refused where it would empty the line it retreats from, which is the case of a line holding nothing but punctuation; a refused retreat leaves the behaviour that existed before this bound and is recorded as such rather than passed over. Nothing here names a publication, a page or a mark: the set of characters that hang is the typesetter's own and is not restated, and the bound is a length.
